name: Middlesex County
seat: No county seat — county government abolished 1997 (Cambridge and Lowell were the historic shire towns)
population_source: 2020 U.S. Census (most populous county in Massachusetts and New England)

officials.name: Peter J. Koutoujian
officials.note: In office since January 2011; runs the Middlesex Jail & House of Correction in Billerica. Funded by the Commonwealth.

officials.name: Marian T. Ryan
officials.note: Middlesex DA since 2013 (a countywide-elected office that predates and survived the 1997 abolition).

officials.name: Karen M. Cassella
officials.note: Took office January 2025, succeeding Richard P. Howe Jr. (register 1995–2024).

officials.name: Tara E. DeCristofaro
officials.note: Countywide-elected; the Probate & Family Court is a unit of the state Trial Court, with sessions in Cambridge and Lowell.

quorum_court.source: Massachusetts abolished Middlesex County government in 1997 (Chapter 48 of the Acts of 1997). There is no county council, board of commissioners, or county executive. The only remaining countywide-elected offices are the Sheriff, District Attorney, Register of Probate, Clerk of Courts, and the two Registers of Deeds — none a general-purpose governing body.

budget_adoption_window.note: The Commonwealth's fiscal year begins July 1; the state budget (which funds the Sheriff) is written in the spring.

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues. Windows to be pinned with local guidance before the voting layer opens.
